judgments.evidence: src/frame.jl:117-176 (_frame_steps!): after frame_top! (the drain, src/sim.jl:2020-2023) the frame loops over spans and steps, and each step end runs run_boundary! then settled!, which publishes (src/sim.jl:2040-2042). The drain-first order holds, but integrate, boundary sequence and publish repeat at every step end and every t*, not once per frame.
judgments.fix: Each frame is one iteration of the loop. The loop runs the drain (the frame-top swap that applies staged device writes to the root inputs), then integrates to each boundary in turn, every step end and every `t*` included, and runs the boundary sequence and publishes at each one ([§10.5][s10-5]).

notes:
I checked all 21 claims against the code at W (detached at f14dbc1d) and changed no tracked file. 18 conform and 3 do not.

- S11a-005 (drift): the frame does drain first. After that, integrate, the boundary sequence and publish repeat at every step end and every t*. They do not run once per frame, as D-445 and D-449 recorded.
- S11a-185 (deviation, backed by D-135): activation(build, T) holds build.lock on every lookup, a cache hit included. Model construction and init! go through that lookup, so sweep workers still synchronize on the lock briefly, even with activations pre-materialized. Two fixes are possible. The code could add a lock-free read once nothing can be inserted, or the doc could be reworded as proposed. The choice is a design ruling, so clear=false.
- S11a-186 (drift): at attach, a path naming no component is refused as PathResolution, not ReadResolution. The docstrings, the tests and spec 11456 already say so. Spec 8200 names ReadResolution alone.

One borderline call: S11a-184 conforms. The staging cell's CAS and swap use Julia's default sequentially consistent order rather than explicit :release/:acquire, and that order includes release/acquire.
